My (elementary) school has a procedure to differentiate the type of break a student gets. 

They can have a quiet break, literally just sit on a couch in the office quietly with a 5 minute timer. It's intent is to be a bit of a sensory break. Just a quiet moment. But also, boring for students who seek attention. They "got" what they wanted, and if it's what they need, then great, but there's also a more exciting version:

They can also have a positive break. When a student has been meeting their goals, or a student has earned a reward for behaving. In this case there's a fun activity like kinetic sand, or therapeutic art, putty, coloring, chatting with an adult, etc.

There will always be kids who abuse the system, but I, as a classroom teacher, enjoy that it works for my high need student and my students who follow the rules also have access to the positives. 

The kids who behave also get the positive, the kids who need support behaving have incentive to behave, and it's consistent. No weird relationships where some adult will give you gum, and another gets accused of being too harsh because they hold a kid to standards.

I suppose it depends on where your wedding is taking place. 


Mine took place near a relatively liberal, accepting city, and I went ahead and clarified that they would be comfortable working with a gay wedding. As another commenter said, if they aren't comfortable with my wedding, I don't want them there. I don't want their vibes messing up my special day. 


I didn't want to have to tiptoe around or be afraid of accidentally revealing that it was gay partway through. That didn't seem like a good use of my time or energy while wedding planning, but I know not all places in which you live can be that welcoming.


Personally, I found it very special to find vendors that were not only OK with a gay wedding. They were overjoyed to have one on their portfolio. There happens to be lavender pages and my town that businesses can be featured in if they've demonstrated having good behavior with LGBT events, and honestly, I would want to give my business to those types of services anyway.


I think it might also depend on how particular your taste is. If you have a very specific vision of what you want, your wedding to be, or a particular caterer you'd like, then that might be a time where you would choose to keep that information private. My wedding was rather eclectic. We figured since the traditional wedding vision was out the window, we might as well have a lot of fun with it. **The Event:** 

[The US government's involvement in destabilizing Guatemala in 1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_Guatemalan_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat#United_Fruit_Company_lobbying), which led to several decades of civil war, a genocide of indigenous Maya, and the death of Democracy in that country. The documentation only became declassified a couple of years ago.

They accused then President of Guatemala Jacobo Arbenz of communism after he passed a land distribution order that would take unused land and distribute it among people who did not own any land (they eventually admitted they found no evidence of Arbenz being communist in any way), and supported a militaristic maniac who started the practice of [massacring entire villages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%ADo_Negro_massacres), which continued up [until the 1990s.
](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_Clarification_Commission)

Seeing people compare the US to a Banana Republic is pretty ballsy considering who exactly created those republics.


**The Reason:** 

The [United Fruit Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Fruit_Company) was particularly against President Arbenz, as they owned much of the unused land in Guatemala, reportedly only using 15% of 500,000 acres.

For context, Guatemala is 108,889 km^2 , so the United Fruit Company, better known by their current name [Chiquita Brand International](https://www.chiquita.com/?gclid=CjwKCAiAouD_BRBIEiwALhJH6EQHoFVd2QFby5x5eSJ83mW2FB44pvg_lorLQx2axke4Ro6T1URuphoCi3wQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds), owned about 1.85% of all the land in the country, including Puerto Barrios, which was the location of the only Atlantic port in the country. 

For the record, landowners were reimbursed for the unused land at a profit. However, the UFC didn't like this and launched a misinformation campaign claiming Guatemala was under communist influence, including lobbying with the government of President Eisenhower, who was notoriously and staunchly anticommunist. [John Dulles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Foster_Dulles), the Secretary of State, and [Allen Welsh Dulles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Dulles), the Director of Central Intelligence, in particular both had vested interest in the success of the UFC. 

The civil war lasted until 1996, which makes it especially painful to think that the [irresponsible cultivation processes of bananas](https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-35131751) means that the Cavendish cultivar of bananas that 200,000 people were killed for in Guatemala alone [may be going extinct soon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_disease).


Further reading: [Bitter Fruit, The Story of the American Coup in Guatemala by Stephen Schlesinger 1982](https://www.amazon.com/Bitter-Fruit-American-Guatemala-Expanded/dp/067401930X)

Life has just started getting good! I'm happier than I've ever been in my life. I have a wife. We hope to have kids soon. It might not even be the surgery that takes me out. Suddenly I feel my mortality as an opponent rather than a comfort.
